# L01: The Triple Hook Method

Unnamed Instagram creator (references Kallaway's hook masterclass) · ig-reel · https://www.instagram.com/p/De_5mQ0R8PE/ · notes: [lessons/01_triple-hook-method.md](../../brain/lessons/01_triple-hook-method.md)

**Core lesson:** A hook nobody skips states the context in the first words (said, shown and written), adds a lean (proof, pain/benefit or shock), then snaps back against the expectation.


## Ideas from this source (14)

- **[Triple hook: context, lean, snapback](../topics/hooks.md#hook-triple-hook-formula)** · hooks: Kallaway-style hook in three steps: context in the first words, a lean that makes the viewer want the next sentence, then a contrarian snapback that yanks them opposite to what they expect (like setting a fishing hook). He calls it the "God-tier hook formula".
- **[Context in the first words, three channels](../topics/hooks.md#hook-context-first-words)** · hooks: Say what the video is about immediately, delivered at once by audio, visuals and on-screen text. The creator claims delaying it even to the back half of the first sentence sharply raises skip rate.
- **[Lean: proof, pain/benefit or shock](../topics/hooks.md#hook-lean-three-ways)** · hooks: After the context, create curiosity with proof (a stat, number, screenshot or result), a specific pain point or benefit, or something shocking (unexpected image, statement or fact).
- **[Claim plus instant visual proof](../topics/hooks.md#hook-bold-claim-visual-proof)** · hooks: Back the opening claim with proof on screen in the first 2–3 s: L01 pairs "scientifically impossible to skip" with a retention graph; L03 shows ROBOT vs PRO animations side by side.
- **[Something new on screen every 1.2–2.5 s](../topics/editing.md#edit-change-every-1-5-2-5s)** · editing: Change something (cut, layout swap, label, card, animation) every 1.5–2.5 s (L01, L02). Rahul measured at roughly every 1.2–2 s in every reel; his sponsored Flipkart reel was the fastest at 1.2 s.
- **[Split layouts: graphic plus face](../topics/editing.md#edit-split-screen-graphic-face)** · editing: Graphic on top, face below, switching to full face for key lines (L01); Rahul's animated top ~55% over a face cam; L04's red step board under the face; long-form: 9:16 examples in rounded windows on the left ~40%, speaker on the right (L06).
- **[A sound on every visual event](../topics/sound.md#sound-sfx-every-event)** · sound: An edit without SFX feels like a "silent movie": put a pop, click, whoosh or snap on every visual change.
- **[SFX meanings: whoosh, pop, chime, thud](../topics/sound.md#sound-sfx-meaning-map)** · sound: Whoosh for movement (slides, wipes, push-ins, window slide-ins), pop for text in, chime for a green check, thud or click for impact or a card change.
- **[Quiet music bed near −22 to −24 dB](../topics/sound.md#sound-quiet-bed-throughout)** · sound: A low ambient synth (L01) or lo-fi/chill-hop (L06) bed runs under the whole video; Oren's sits at about −22 to −24 dB under the voice, with SFX on top.
- **[Frosted cards, drawn diagrams, red arrows](../topics/effects.md#fx-frosted-glass-cards)** · effects: Frosted-glass UI cards (L01, L02), drawn diagrams (curves, radar, fishing line) and red circles/arrows that guide the eye (L01).
- **[Teaching text: clean sans, red/green](../topics/text.md#text-clean-sans-teaching)** · text: Clean sans (Inter / SF Pro style), white and yellow on dark; red = bad/wrong (or price up), green = good/right (or saved).
- **[Dark matte background, warm key, gold rim](../topics/colour.md#colour-dark-matte-warm-key)** · colour: L01's look: dark matte background, warm key light on the face, gold rim light.
- **[Talking-head light and lens looks](../topics/filming.md#film-talking-head-lighting)** · filming: Soft key front-left with a 35–50 mm wide-aperture look (L06); warm key with gold rim (L01); 20–24 mm wide for energy (L07); high-key soft 3-point with rim for a podcast (L08).
- **[Comment KEYWORD and I'll send it](../topics/growth.md#growth-comment-keyword-cta)** · growth: "Comment 'hooks' and I'll send it to you": a comment-to-DM freebie, with social proof (700K views) raising its value. Rahul uses it on nearly every reel with the keyword in the caption and as a big yellow label in the last 2–4 s.
